data.old_pc_link: The PC-Link is older than generation 3

data_description.feedback_module: Its own reads of the modules are then picked up, and Home Assistant only reads what it leaves out. Leave off when the serial cable is on the Feedback Module itself.
data_description.old_pc_link: Such a PC-Link answers no state read. Home Assistant then reads nothing: an output shows what Home Assistant last wrote to it, kept across restarts, and stays unknown until it is written once. A command also sets the other outputs of the same group of six to what Home Assistant last wrote.
data_description.press_repeat: How many times a press sent by Home Assistant repeats its telegram, as a held key does. Three is what a module needs to count one press; raise it only if presses from Home Assistant are sometimes missed.

data_description.output: The roller output to set up.

shutter_settings.title: A roller output
shutter_settings.description: The module's own links run this output {open} to open and {close} to close. Leave a time empty to use that. An end margin left empty is {margin}.

data_description.use_as: A shutter, or a load wired to the output's first relay, shown as a switch or a light. Changing this removes the entity it had.
data_description.open_time: How long the shutter takes from closed to open. The position is estimated from it.
data_description.close_time: How long the shutter takes from open to closed.
data_description.end_margin: How long the motor is left running past a fully open or closed estimate, so the shutter reaches its end stop.

names.title: Names from the project file
names.description: Upload the .nkb project of the Nikobus software to take the names it holds for modules, plates, outputs and light scenes. Names you gave in Home Assistant are kept.

data_description.rooms_as_areas: Modules and plates that have no area are put in the area named like their room in the project; the area is created when it does not exist. Outputs have no room in the project.
data_description.use_as_inventory: For an installation without a PC-Link: the modules and plates are taken from the project file instead, replacing what is known, and the links are then read from the modules. That takes a few minutes; the entry reloads when it ends.

data_description.light_outputs: The relay outputs that switch a lamp. Each becomes a light entity instead of a switch; its switch entity is removed, with the name and area you gave it.
data_description.fan_outputs: The dimmer outputs that drive a variable-speed fan. Each becomes a fan entity with a speed instead of a light; its light entity is removed, with the name and area you gave it.

data_description.output: The output that Home Assistant is to switch by pressing a key, so that the LED of that key follows.

led_key_settings.title: LED keys of an output
led_key_settings.description: A plate's LED follows the telegrams of its key, not an output written directly. With a key set here, Home Assistant switches the output by that key: it reads the module first and leaves the key alone when the output is already there. Offered are the keys linked to this output; another address can be typed. Leave both empty to write the output directly again.

data_description.on_key: For a shutter: the key that opens it. A key that toggles can be given for both.
data_description.off_key: For a shutter: the key that closes it.

module_type.title: The type of a module
module_type.description: For a module the inventory holds as another type than it is. Its entities change to match, and its links are read again by themselves once the integration has reloaded, since they are decoded by type. The choice stays through later discoveries.

data_description.module: Each module with the type it has now.

files.title: Inventory from two files
files.description: For an installation with neither a PC-Link nor a project file: the two files of the Nikobus integration, one listing the modules and their outputs, the other the keys. They replace what is known. What they say of an output (light, fan, LED keys, run times) becomes the matching option here. The links are then read from the modules, which takes a few minutes.

take_over.title: Take over from the Nikobus integration
take_over.description:
{entities} entities of the Nikobus integration have a counterpart here: its lights, switches, covers, fans, scenes and input switches. Submitting moves each one's entity ID, name as shown, area, aliases, labels, icon and voice-assistant exposure onto this integration's entity, so dashboards, automations and history keep working. {lights} relays become lights here to match.

The Nikobus entities are kept, parked under their ID followed by `_nikobus`, and **Give back** undoes all of it.

Not taken over: {left} other Nikobus entities, mostly its key sensors and press buttons, which are event entities here. Automations that use those, or the Nikobus bus events and actions by name, have to be changed by hand.

Keep the Nikobus entry disabled: only one program may talk to the bus.

give_back.title: Give back to the Nikobus integration
give_back.description: {entities} entities were taken over. Submitting gives each Nikobus entity its entity ID back, and this integration's entities the IDs they had before. Names, areas and aliases stay as they are on both.

error.invalid_project_file: This file could not be read as a Nikobus project.
error.invalid_key_address: A key address is six hexadecimal digits, for example 0B7086.
error.invalid_files: The two files could not be read as a module list and a key list. Check that each is valid JSON, that every module has an address and the number of outputs of its type, and that every key has an address.

abort.bus_taken: A discovery or a check is running. Try again when it has ended.
abort.nikobus_running: The Nikobus integration is running. Disable its entry first: only one program may talk to the bus, and its entities are in use.

not_connected.message: The Nikobus gateway is not connected.

no_pc_link.message: No PC-Link answered the inventory. Without a PC-Link, upload the .nkb project in the options (Names from the project file) and use it as the inventory.

no_modules.message: The PC-Link holds no output module.

maintenance_running.message: A check or a backup of the programming is running.

backup_failed.message: The backup could not be written to {path}: {error}

not_loaded.message: The Nikobus NG integration is not loaded.

unknown_module.message: No output module has the address {address}.

rgb_no_key.message: No key that switches RGB controller {address} is known. The keys linked to it are in the project file only: upload the .nkb in the options.

zone_function_missing.message: This function is not programmed on this zone.

llm_not_an_output.message: {entity_id} is not an output of this Nikobus installation.

llm_not_a_key.message: {key} is not a key of this Nikobus installation.

module_memory_error.title: {module} reports a memory error
module_memory_error.description:
The module answered its status request with its memory-error flag set. Its programming may be damaged, and its keys may stop working as programmed.

1. Open the installation in the Nikobus software and send the programming to this module again.
2. Press **Check programming** on the Nikobus device in Home Assistant.

This notice goes away when the check finds the flag cleared.

module_checksum_mismatch.title: The memory of {module} does not match its checksum
module_checksum_mismatch.description:
Home Assistant read the whole memory of the module and computed another checksum than the one the module reports. Either a byte was read wrongly on the bus, or the module's memory is damaged.

1. Press **Check programming** on the Nikobus device again; a read error does not repeat.
2. If the notice stays, send the programming to this module again from the Nikobus software, then check once more.

This notice goes away when a check finds both checksums equal.

module_type_mismatch.title: {module} is not the type the inventory says
module_type_mismatch.description:
The inventory holds this module as a {module_type}, but it answers as a {family}. Its outputs are then shown as the wrong kind of entity.

1. Press **Discover installation** on the Nikobus device, so the inventory is read from the PC-Link again.
2. Press **Check programming** afterwards.

This notice goes away when the check finds the two agree. If it stays, please report the module's model in an issue.

confirm.title: {module} was reprogrammed
confirm.description:
The module's memory has changed since Home Assistant read its links, so what Home Assistant knows of its keys, run times and scenes may be out of date.

Submit to read this module's links again. It takes a minute or two, during which Home Assistant does not follow the outputs; the entry reloads when it ends.

abort.bus_taken: A discovery or a check is already running. Try again when it has ended.

confirm.title: {module} does not answer
confirm.description:
The module has not answered three reads in a row while other modules did, so its entities show an old state. Check its power and its bus wiring first; this notice goes away by itself when it answers again.

If the module was taken out of the installation, submit to remove it and its entities from Home Assistant. It stays removed through later discoveries, even while the PC-Link still lists it. The **Discover** action with its address brings it back.

module_corrupt_links.title: The link table of {module} could not be read
module_corrupt_links.description:
The links stored in this module do not line up the way a link table does, so they were skipped: Home Assistant does not know which keys drive its outputs. The Nikobus software reports the same and asks for the module to be reprogrammed.

1. Open the installation in the Nikobus software and send the programming to this module again.
2. Run the **Discover** action for this module, or press **Discover installation** on the Nikobus device.

This notice goes away when its links are read cleanly.

no_device_answered.title: Nothing answered on {connection}
no_device_answered.description:
The connection opened, but no Nikobus device answered on it, so no state is read and every command will time out.

1. Check that this is the port of the PC-Link, and that the PC-Link has power.
2. Close the Nikobus software if it is running: only one program can use the port.
3. If another program used the port before, unplug the PC-Link's power for a few seconds.

This notice goes away by itself as soon as a Nikobus frame is received. To use another port, reconfigure the integration.

feedback_module_port.title: Home Assistant is on the Feedback Module's own port

confirm.title: Home Assistant is on the Feedback Module's own port
confirm.description:
The Feedback Module option is on, but its state answers arrive without the queries behind them. Only a PC-Link relays both; the Feedback Module's own port relays the answers alone. Home Assistant then has to guess which half of a module an answer is for, and the two halves of a twelve-output module get swapped.

Submit to turn the option off. Home Assistant then reads the modules itself, every two minutes and after each key press, and the integration reloads.

module_type_fixable.title: {module} is not the type the inventory says

confirm.title: {module} is not the type the inventory says
confirm.description:
The inventory holds this module as a {module_type}, but it answers as a {family}. Its outputs are then shown as the wrong kind of entity, and its links are decoded the wrong way.

Submit to treat it as a {family}. The integration reloads, the module's entities change to match (the old ones are removed), and its links are read again, which takes a minute or two.

press_key.name: Press a key
press_key.description: Puts the telegram of a key on the bus, as a press of that key does. Works for an address no plate of the inventory has, such as a function of the Nikobus software.

address.name: Address
address.description: The six hexadecimal digits the key sends, as shown on its event entity.

read_module.name: Read a module
read_module.description: Reads the outputs of one module now, or of every module, instead of waiting for the next periodic read.

address.name: Module
address.description: The four hexadecimal digits of the module. Empty reads every module.

verify_programming.name: Check programming
verify_programming.description: Reads each module's status and whole memory and compares its checksum. Read-only; takes minutes. Returns the result per module.

modules.name: Modules
modules.description: Module addresses to check. Empty checks every output module.

backup_programming.name: Back up programming
backup_programming.description: Checks the modules and writes the memory of each to a dated folder under nikobus_ng_backup in the configuration directory. Read-only; takes minutes. Returns the folder and the result per module.

modules.name: Modules
modules.description: Module addresses to back up. Empty backs up every output module.

discover.name: Discover
discover.description: Reads the installation again from the bus: the PC-Link's inventory and every module's links, or only the links of one module. Runs in the background and reloads the integration when it ends. Read-only.

address.name: Module
address.description: The four hexadecimal digits of a module, to read only its links again, for instance after reprogramming it. Empty reads the whole installation.

describe.name: Describe the installation
describe.description: Returns the installation as data: every output with the keys that drive it, their modes and times, every key with what it drives, the scenes with their outputs, the logical inputs and the health of the bus. Read from what the discovery stored; nothing is sent on the bus.
